Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the pre-operative image (Figure 1a), which shows a relatively normal mediastinum, to the post-operative image (Figure 3a), there is a marked increase in the width of the superior mediastinum. In the context of a thyroid angiosarcoma, this rapid enlargement of the mediastinal mass is most indicative of aggressive tumor recurrence rather than a stable post-surgical change or hematoma.
